## UPS Without Replacement {#sec-ups-wo}

### Review of UPSWR and the Horvitz--Thompson Estimator {#sec-ups-wo-theory}

**Review of UPSWR in terms of $\psi_i$.** With replacement, each of the $n$ draws selects unit $i$ with
probability $\psi_i$, and draw $j$ gives the unbiased estimate $y_j^*/\psi_j^*$ of the total $t$, since
$E(y_j^*/\psi_j^*)=\sum_i\psi_i\,y_i/\psi_i=t$. The HH estimator averages the $n$ estimates,
$$
\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HH}}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{y_j^*}{\psi_j^*},\qquad
\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HH}})=\frac{s_u}{\sqrt{n}},\qquad
s_u^2=\frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{j=1}^n\left(\frac{y_j^*}{\psi_j^*}-\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HH}}\right)^2 ,
$$
where the SE is easy because the $n$ estimates are iid. With $\psi_i=x_i/t_x$, $\frac{y_j^*}{\psi_j^*}=t_x\,b_j^*$,
which gives the estimator $\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HH}}=t_x\bar{b}^*$ of @sec-ups-hh-theory. The drawback of
UPSWR is that a large unit can be drawn several times, which is wasteful.

**Without replacement.** Now $n$ **distinct** units are selected, and the design is described by the
**inclusion probabilities**
$$
\pi_i=P(\text{unit } i\in\mathcal{S}),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^N\pi_i=n ,
$$
for a sample of fixed size $n$. For a size variable $x_i$, we take $\pi_i=n\,x_i/t_x$ (inclusion probability
proportional to size, $\pi$ps), which is $n\psi_i$ for $\psi_i=x_i/t_x$. A unit with $n\,x_i/t_x>1$ is
included with certainty, $\pi_i=1$, and the other probabilities are recomputed from the remaining units.

**The Horvitz--Thompson (HT) estimator.** Weighting each sampled unit by $1/\pi_i$ gives
$$
\boxed{\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}=\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}} .
$$
It has the same form as the HH estimator with $n\psi_i$ replaced by $\pi_i$ (the two coincide if no unit is
drawn twice). *It is unbiased.* Let $I_i=1$ if unit $i$ is in the sample and $0$ otherwise, so that
$E(I_i)=P(I_i=1)=\pi_i$. Then $\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}=\sum_{i=1}^N I_i\,y_i/\pi_i$, and
$$
E(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}\,E(I_i)=\sum_{i=1}^N\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}\,\pi_i=\sum_{i=1}^N y_i=t .
$$
This needs only $\pi_i>0$ for all units. The estimator of the mean per unit is
$\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}/N$. When the inclusion probabilities are proportional to a size variable $x_i$,
$\pi_i=n\,x_i/t_x$, the estimator of the ratio $B=t/t_x$ is, as for UPSWR, the HT total divided by $t_x$,
$$
\hat{B}_{\mathrm{HT}}=\frac{\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}}{t_x}=\frac{1}{t_x}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}
=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\frac{y_i}{x_i}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}b_i ,
$$
the plain average of the ratios $b_i=y_i/x_i$ of the $n$ sampled units, with
$\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat{B}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\widehat{\mathrm{SE}}(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})/t_x$. In cluster sampling, $y_i=t_i$ and
$x_i=M_i$, so that $\hat{B}_{\mathrm{HT}}=\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}/M_0$ is the mean per element
(@sec-ups-cluster-theory).

**Variances.** For a fixed sample size, with the joint inclusion probabilities $\pi_{ij}=P(i,j\in\mathcal{S})$,
$$
V(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{j=1}^N(\pi_i\pi_j-\pi_{ij})
\left(\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}-\frac{y_j}{\pi_j}\right)^2
\qquad\text{(Sen--Yates--Grundy)},
$$
which is estimated unbiasedly by summing over the sampled pairs only, each divided by $\pi_{ij}$:
$$
\hat{V}_{\mathrm{SYG}}(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\sum_{j\in\mathcal{S}}
\frac{\pi_i\pi_j-\pi_{ij}}{\pi_{ij}}\left(\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}-\frac{y_j}{\pi_j}\right)^2 .
$$
The joint probabilities $\pi_{ij}$ are hard to compute for most sampling methods, so approximations that need
only $\pi_i$ are used:

* **Hájek's approximation** (for designs with high entropy), obtained by
  $\pi_{ij}\approx\pi_i\pi_j\left[1-\frac{(1-\pi_i)(1-\pi_j)}{\sum_k\pi_k(1-\pi_k)}\right]$ in the SYG estimator:
  $$
  \hat{V}_{\mathrm{H}}(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\frac{n}{n-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}(1-\pi_i)
  \left(\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}-A\right)^2,\qquad
  A=\frac{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}(1-\pi_i)\,y_i/\pi_i}{\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}(1-\pi_i)} .
  $$

* **With-replacement approximation:** treat the sample as $n$ draws with $\psi_i=\pi_i/n$ and use the
  UPSWR formula,
  $$
  \hat{V}_{\mathrm{WR}}(\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}})=\frac{n}{n-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\left(\frac{y_i}{\pi_i}-\frac{\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}}{n}\right)^2 .
  $$
  It ignores the factors $1-\pi_i$ that account for sampling without replacement, so it overestimates the
  variance, the more so the larger the $\pi_i$.

For the mean per unit, divide the estimate and the SE by $N$; for the ratio $\hat{B}_{\mathrm{HT}}$, divide by $t_x$.

### Example: Acres of Farmland in Counties (`agpop.csv`) {#sec-ups-wo-example}

We draw a sample of $n=100$ of the counties of `agpop` without replacement, with inclusion probabilities
$\pi_i=100\,x_i/t_x$ proportional to the acres in 1987 ($x_i$), and estimate the mean acres of farmland in 1992
($y_i$) per county. (The few counties with no farmland in 1987 cannot be selected and are left out.) The sample
is drawn by maximum entropy sampling, a fixed-size design with these inclusion probabilities, from the R package
`sampling`; a county with $100x_i/t_x>1$ would be included with certainty (none is here).


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(sampling)
agpop <- acres_in_thousands(read.csv("data/agpop.csv", na.strings = "-99"))
agpop <- agpop |> filter(!is.na(acres92), !is.na(acres87), acres87 > 0)
N <- nrow(agpop)
n <- 100
tx <- sum(agpop$acres87)
pik <- inclusionprobabilities(agpop$acres87, n)    # pi_i = n x_i / t_x

set.seed(348)
q_me <- UPMEqfromw(UPMEpiktildefrompik(pik), n)    # set-up of the sampling design
s <- which(UPMEsfromq(q_me) == 1)                  # indices of the n sampled counties
y <- agpop$acres92[s]; x <- agpop$acres87[s]; p <- pik[s]
```
:::


The mean per county, estimated by HT with the two variance estimators (the plain sample mean ignores the
inclusion probabilities and is shown for contrast), and the ratio $\hat{B}_{\mathrm{HT}}=\hat{t}_{\mathrm{HT}}/t_x$,
the acres in 1992 per acre in 1987:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
est_ht_hajek <- upswo_est(y, p, N, method = "mean", variance = "hajek")
est_ht_wr    <- upswo_est(y, p, N, method = "mean", variance = "wr")
est_B_hajek <- upswo_est(y, p, N, tx, method = "ratio", variance = "hajek")
est_B_wr    <- upswo_est(y, p, N, tx, method = "ratio", variance = "wr")
```
:::


To judge the variance estimators, we repeat the sampling 2000 times, and compute the standard deviation of the
2000 HT estimates, which is the true standard error of the design, and the average of the estimated standard
errors:


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
R <- 2000
sim <- matrix(0, R, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, c("est", "se_hajek", "se_wr")))
for (i in 1:R) {
  si <- which(UPMEsfromq(q_me) == 1)
  sim[i, ] <- c(upswo_est(agpop$acres92[si], pik[si], N, method = "mean", variance = "hajek")[1:2],
                upswo_est(agpop$acres92[si], pik[si], N, method = "mean", variance = "wr")[2])
}
```
:::
